To implement pagination with Kaminari, first ensure the gem is in your Gemfile: `gem 'kaminari'`. ### 1. Controller Implementation Update the controller to use `.page` and `.per(10)`. ```ruby # app/controllers/articles_controller.rb class ArticlesController < ApplicationController def index # Kaminari methods can be chained directly onto ActiveRecord relations @articles = Article.all.page(params[:page]).per(10) end end ``` ### 2. View Implementation (Helper Methods) Add the navigation links in your view to allow users to switch pages. ```erb <%# app/views/articles/index.html.erb %>

Articles

<% @articles.each do |article| %> <% end %>
Title Content
<%= article.title %> <%= article.content %>
<%= paginate_arrows @articles %>
``` ### 3. Optional: Customizing the View (Optional) If you want to customize the HTML of the pagination links, you can create a partial or override the helper in your `application_helper.rb`. ```ruby # app/helpers/application_helper.rb module ApplicationHelper def paginate_arrows(collection) paginate_default_partial(collection) end end ```
